definition: Operations means the logical task operations declared by the immutable temporal workload packet. Physical queries, routing, traversal, normalization and refusal costs are measured candidate implementation changes.

hunks.assessment: Comments document hazards; imports provide exact arithmetic, errors and path counting. No operation descriptor, input data or schedule edit.
Types add explicit closure seeds and reusable reachability selector. Seeds bound the implementation to the same task start; no operation/data/schedule edit.
Session type exposes both closure-language selectors and supported language names. This selects the native implementation; no operation/data/schedule edit.
XTQL integer and attribute-view helpers translate the existing fact filters. No input values, parameter meaning or schedule changes.

Execute/closure helpers add explicit language dispatch, task-wide source-position capture, same contract parameter typing, seeded read-only traversal and a mark-join hazard refusal. Unset routing stays XTQL state reads and SQL otherwise. Additional reads, per-round execution, refusal limits and client work are candidate costs. Requested logical operations, requested valid/recorded cuts, fixture data and offered schedule stay fixed; multi-call coherence is an implementation correctness fix.
Workload 03 purchase-time query gains equivalent XTQL and retains SQL joins/filters. Purchases and at-purchase price requests are unchanged; no data/schedule edit.

Workload 04 coordinate and coverage queries gain XTQL equivalents. The same claim, coverage, policy and event-derived valid subcut feed the existing existence operation. No operation/data/schedule edit.

Workload 05 distinct accepted-event count and highest-revision status gain XTQL; 06/07 replace unsafe aggregate arithmetic with exact split sums and typed overflow. Same account/currency/SKU/ledger operands, grouping and requested outputs. Correct arithmetic/refusal behavior changes execution, not operation definitions, data or schedule.

Workload 07 final subtraction uses typed int64 failure; 08 implements the same capture-minus-refund total exactly; 09 SQL correlated predicates use IS TRUE and gains XTQL; 10 gains XTQL for unchanged deadline/completion/watermark steps. No operation/data/schedule edit; client normalization and native query costs remain measured.

Workloads 11/13/14/15 and 20 closure dispatch use seeded read-only closure and same joins/targets; 13 adds a hazard guard; 12 gains XTQL and SQL null-hazard correction; 16 retains its input/metadata lineage reads in both languages; 17 gains XTQL for the same ordered three-step conversion and bounds. Branch relocation does not remove any operation. Physical traversal, intermediate rows and guard reads change; logical operations/data/schedule do not.

Workload 17 builder closes unchanged SQL assembly; 18 adds equivalent XTQL interval endpoint segmentation and fixes SQL correlated-null predicates; 19 switches to the shared execute helper. Same clipping bounds and recorded-fact relation, union-duration operation and prediction lookup; no input data or schedule change.

Workload 19 adds XTQL for the same customer/predicted-at/feature-known-at/fraud projection, retaining the SQL and subsequent historical feature reads. Requested logical subcuts and parameters remain unchanged; no operation/data/schedule edit.

Workload 20 closure moved to the common closure branch above; support counting replaces three length-1..3 SQL counts with one distinct-edge extraction plus bounded general simple-path counting. The immutable fixture is the acyclic A-B/C-D diamond with edge retirements and path counts 2/1/0, so the requested operation/result meaning stays identical. Query count, intermediate volume, limits and host cost change and are measured. No fixture data, requested cut or offered schedule edit.
Imports the shared bounded path-count helper. No operation/data/schedule edit.

Allows a caller-specific maxRows, keeping the previous 1000 default for all existing calls. The support-edge scan requests a completeness witness up to SUPPORT_EDGE_LIMIT+1. No logical operation, source data or schedule edit.
Passes the selected row cap to the native query. This is execution admission/completeness handling; no operation/data/schedule edit.

Workload 20 replaces three fixed-length SPARQL witness counts with distinct-edge extraction and bounded general simple-path counting over the same graph, endpoints and captured task cut. The frozen A/B/C/D diamond and its 2/1/0 expected counts are unchanged. Query sequence/volume/client cost/refusal behavior change; the requested support-count operation, data and offered schedule do not.

decision: ELIGIBLE-FOR-REPIN; no frozen logical operation, data or offered schedule change
